title: Count Orders Grouped by Year and Month
description:
Group orders by calendar year and month to see how many were placed each month.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `amount`, `order_date`

Return `year`, `month`, and `order_count`. Order by `year`, `month`.
solution_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) AS year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

test_cases.description: 3 year-month groups: Jan(3 orders), Feb(3), Mar(4)

hints: Use EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) and EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) to decompose the date.
GROUP BY 1, 2 is shorthand for grouping by the 1st and 2nd SELECT expressions.
explanation: EXTRACT splits a date into components. Grouping by both year and month creates one row per calendar month. January has orders 1–3 (count=3), February has 4–6 (count=3), March has 7–10 (count=4).
